newsitem.title: USA: FPL commits orimulsion to EPA proposal.
newsitem.headline: FPL commits orimulsion to EPA proposal.

text.p: Florida Power & Light Co said Thursday engineering and test results demonstrate its Manatee power plant, when converted to orimulsion, can meet newly proposed, tougher federal standards for nitrogen oxide emissions.

If the stricter standards are passed, the FPL Group Inc subsidiary said, it will comply with them using Orimulsion, even though the Manatee plant, as an existing facility under both Florida Department of environmental Protection and Environmental Protection Agency rules, is not subject to the proposed rate.

Orimulsion is a mixture of water and very low gravity crude oil from Venezuela's Orinco Tar Belt that would be produced in a $320 million processing plant planned by DuPont Co's Conoco Inc, Norway's Statoil and Venezuela's Bitumenes de Orininoco. The group plans to start work on a five million metric tonne per year plant this year.
FPL'S proposal to convert its Mantee power plant to orimulsion will again be reviewed by the state's Power Plant Siting Board on September 9, a utility spokesman said.
The board, consisting of Gov. Lawton Chiles and the cabinet, rejected the project by a 4-3 vote in April 1996, citing concerns of Mantee county and the Tampa Bay region.

In May, a state appeals court ruled the plan should get a second consideration, stating the board could override the positive findings of a state hearing officer only if those finds "were based on competent substantial evidence."

As a condition of its orimulsion permit, FPL said in a statement Thurssday, it would reduce the power plant's NOx rate to 0.15 pounds per million BTU from 0.23 pounds per million BTU. That is the rate proposed by EPA to ensure continued protection of human health and welfare.
The utility noted the 228 megawatt Manatee plant currently uses residual fuel oil, and its permit limits the NOx emission rate to 0.30 pounds per million BTU.
